findings.evidence: version_guard states 'the problem must stay in the stated four-problem deck', but SPEC.md (SOURCE 3) says 'deck stays at three since 2026-11-09' and 'Problem 04 (grid + MinGRU RL sim SPS) was retired 2026-11-09'; SOURCE 2 leaderboard.json lists exactly three problems (01, 02, 03). A changed task set cannot silently reuse the identity (c1).
findings.repair: Rewrite version_guard to reference the current three-problem deck (01 glm52_fused_moe, 02 deepseek_nsa, 03 megaqwen_decode) and note problem 04 was retired 2026-11-09.

findings.repair: Remove or explicitly date-stamp the problem-04 references as pre-retirement context (e.g. 'until the 2026-11-09 retirement'), so no current cross-check claim rests on cells the board no longer publishes.

uncertainties: c1 metric/unit/range: row's stated mapping (peak_fraction × 100 as the context column for problem 02 under SPEC.md's latency-anchored standing rule) matches SOURCE 3, and SOURCE 7's served-value scale (23 values, min 2.51, max 136.19) matches leaderboard fractions ×100 (0.0251 min, 1.3619 max), so unit 'percent of roofline' and range [0,null] (unbounded upper) agree with the served scale. The claim that peak_fraction is a percentage of a roofline for problem 02, while SPEC calls the roofline ceiling 'structurally unreadable' there, rests on the row's own choice to publish the context column; judged only on scale, it is consistent.

c2 version_status 'published': the maintainer publishes 'RTX_PRO_6000' as the hardware identifier (SOURCE 5, SOURCE 2 hardware.name), which the version copies; no dated release identifier for the board appears in the packet, so 'published' vs 'snapshot' depends on reading the hardware identifier as the maintainer's release identifier for the board.
